# Deckard 1.8.0 - Deckard tells you when there is a newer version

Deckard now checks whether a newer release exists and tells you when it does.

## What is new

- **Update banner.** When Deckard starts it looks, in the background, for a newer version. If there is one, a box appears at the bottom of the navigation rail saying "Deckard 1.9.0 is available" (the number is whatever the new version is). It pulses for a few seconds to catch your eye, then stays still. Hover over its button to see a short note on what is new, and press **See what's new** to open the release page in your browser, where you can download the new zip.
- **Quiet when there is nothing to say.** If you are up to date, offline, behind a proxy that blocks it, or the check fails for any reason, you see nothing at all and Deckard opens as normal. The check never delays the window.
- **Nothing about you is sent.** Deckard only reads one small public file. It sends no name, machine, address or usage information.

## Things to know

- **Install this version by hand once.** Earlier versions have no update check, so they will never show the banner. From 1.8.0 on you are told about each new release.
- **Notify only.** Deckard does not download or install the new version itself. The button opens the release page and you replace the folder as you do now. The release page is on GitHub, so you need to be signed in to an account that can see the repository.
- **No switch yet.** The check runs every time Deckard starts and there is no setting to turn it off or to limit it to once a day. The command line programs (`Deckard.Cli.exe`, the MCP server) never check.
